items.summary: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins. Brain scans revealed that two regions involved in memory and emotion start shrinking before the hippocampus, the area doctors typically examine for signs of Alzheimer’s. These early changes are linked to abnormal tau protein buildup and could provide a powerful new way to identify people at risk.

Hence the excitement over the discovery in northern China of some of the oldest known rocks on Earth, dating back 3.95 billion years. And one of the reasons for all the attention is that they're revealing new clues about how Earth's crust formed and evolved.

Driving the news: Duffy explained that the outage was caused when a contractor performed routine maintenance on a telecommunications line to upgrade a copper wire to fiber-optic cable and install a new router. "It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued, meaning that line was going to get shut down. So we had to switch it over from old copper," Duffy said. Too much light exposure during sleep may lead to potentially harmful changes in the structure and function of the heart, a new study suggests. Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 10, 2026, 5:26 PM EDT By Barbara Mantel Exposure to light during nighttime sleep may lead to potentially harmful changes in the structure and function of the heart, according to a study published Wednesday in the European Heart Journal. Previous research had shown a link between nighttime sleep while exposed to light and an elevated risk of coronary artery disease , heart attack, heart failure and stroke. The new study is the first to examine how it also affects the structure and function of the heart.

Molly Callahan, a gynecological teaching assistant, helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams On her busiest days, Molly Callahan, has 16 speculums inserted into her vagina. She works full-time as a gynecological teaching assistant ( GTA ) – a layperson who helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams before they work with actual patients. It’s not as unpleasant as you might think. In fact, the point is to help students learn how to do it without causing discomfort. Contrary to common belief, pap smears – tests that screen for cervical cancer – don’t have to be painful.

Men aged 50–69 and at average risk should get PSA screening every two years. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. Cost and access barriers are pushing people to modified use and unapproved versions. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That’s around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

(AP) — Christian Watson just had to stay healthy. Matthew Golden simply required a few more targets. Both are getting just what they needed, and it's helped the Green Bay Packers duo develop into one of the NFL's top receiving tandems. Watson ranks fourth (97.7) and Golden eighth (87.0) in yards receiving per game, making them the only teammates in the top 10. Watson has 49 catches for 879 yards and seven touchdowns, while Golden has 53 receptions for 783 yards and five scores. "Having a little bit more defined roles this season has allowed us to go out there and be who we are as players, as individuals," Watson said. "We're kind of just feeding off of each other."

Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night's loss to the Commanders. To win a Senate seat in a highly polarized, deeply Republican state, Scott Colom needed a perfect storm. He got it. A new nonprofit in Charlotte is looking to get more kids on the soccer field, and it’s all thanks to a Charlotte teen. Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text – much of it in an obsolete shorthand – which is now said to contain hundreds of proved theorems The Austrian logician Kurt Gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century. His two incompleteness theorems , published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age. After his seminal results of the 1930s, Gödel published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science.

In the meta-analysis, a few drugs stood out for offering greater effectiveness over time. A new meta-analysis found that certain antidepressants worked better on average than Prozac at helping people with depression feel better and stick with their treatment over the long term. The analysis looked at 21 different drugs across 115 studies to identify which drugs were most likely to help patients who planned to use antidepressants for more than three months. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called Friday's sudden FAA ground stoppage "unprecedented" but said there's no indication yet of an attack. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin called the sudden ground stop of all U.S. flights Friday evening “unprecedented,” but insisted the frightening incident was “not another 9/11.” Speaking to reporters Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration suddenly issued the full ground stoppage, which bans planes from taking off, Mullin pinned the blame on a “telecommunications issue.”

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said during the intermittent outage, controllers could still reach pilots. A communications outage on Friday led the Federal Aviation Administration to pause departing flights nationwide, but pilots were not entirely cut off from federal air traffic controllers. In a Friday night news conference, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outage was intermittent, so federal controllers were still able to reach pilots. “It wasn’t a complete blackout in communication or radar,” he said. “So we were able to keep some of those communications going.”

Find out how a deck of playing cards can create a fun, challenging putting drill that improves every aspect of your game on the green. This simple twist will transform any ordinary practice session into a fun, competitive challenge that tests every aspect of your game on the green. To try it out, all you need is a standard deck of playing cards, a practice green with a few holes to putt to and a way to record your score. Start by splitting the cards into two decks: face cards (plus aces) and numbered cards. Next, shuffle both decks of cards. Each card will dictate three characteristics of your putt: distance, direction and slope.

When Unix was being developed, the team needed a reference date to help calculate time. Low and behold, January 1, 1970, was chosen. Brianajackson/Getty Images Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover There's a good chance you've seen the date January 1, 1970 on a computer or other device, even if you weren't alive back then. Wondering what an NPU actually does and whether you even need it? We Quality Stock Arts/Shutterstock Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Bought a new laptop recently? Chances are that it's equipped with an NPU, a chip you're almost certainly not using. The NPU, or Neural Processing Unit, is a block of silicon that runs AI workloads at a fraction of the power a CPU or GPU needs. Roughly 2W compared to well over 100W that standard laptop discrete graphics need to do the same job. While they're not yet found in all laptops, they're now pretty much standard in mid-range and premium machines.

The away goals tiebreaker may not be used in Europe anymore, but it's still up and running in Concacaf. The Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals take place over the next several days, with four semifinal spots on the line. The quarterfinals will be staged over two legs, with each team hosting a match. If the aggregate score is tied after 180 minutes of play, the team with more away goals will advance. Away goals scored during extra time do not serve as an additional tiebreaker, so if the teams remain level after extra time, the series goes to penalties.

Multiple boys sports saw participation decreases in two time periods within the past three calendar years. Football took a big hit with a 9% drop in participation from 2024-2025 to 2025-2026. There were 8,831 boys playing football in 2024-2025, but 8,015 in 2025-2026. Overall, Connecticut saw over 4% fewer participants in 2025-2026 than it did in 2024-2025, according to CIAC numbers. There were 58,605 boys who played sports in 2024-2025, but that decreased to 55,990 in 2025-2026. Six-percent decreases were seen in swimming and indoor track. Swimming declined from 1,606 boys in 2024-2025 to 1,513 in 2025-2026. Indoor track fell from 5,703 boys in 2024-2025 to 5,387 in 2025-2026.

The decision led to a hasty appeals process and an eventual petition for emergency relief in state Supreme Court that was withdrawn Friday.

The NFL's new player safety policy brings one-game suspensions for repeat violations, but no Buccaneers appear on the latest watch list. The NFL and NFL Players Association announced the changes on August 26, establishing a disciplinary system targeting five specific violations: hip-drop tackles, horse-collar tackles, launching, hits on defenseless players, and blindside blocks. Players who commit three violations of the same designated rule face a one-game suspension, making repeated dangerous techniques a potential personnel concern rather than simply a financial penalty.

On what some might call a divinely orchestrated day, I had what remains my most surreal experience at an Arsenal game.I can remember it as clear as daylight. Despite handling the most flights in the world, the United States’ air traffic systems rely on 1980s-era computer equipment. Stop mindlessly hitting putts. A simple deck of cards creates real pressure and exposes weak spots in your short game according to Golf.com. Chris George, a teacher featured by Golf.com , outlines a drill that uses a standard deck to dictate every shot. The setup is easy. Split the cards into two piles: face cards plus aces, and the numbered cards. Shuffle both. The card drawn sets the distance, the direction, and the slope. Numbered cards show the feet for the putt. Face cards have fixed lengths: Jacks are 15 feet, Queens are 20, Kings are 25, and Aces stretch to 35 feet.

The Ducks were scheduled to host Pepperdine on Sunday afternoon inside Matthew Arena, but the Waves were unable to make it to Eugene in time, and the game has been postponed. Whether the game has been postponed permanently is yet to be seen, but for right now, both schools are looking for an appropriate date to make up the game. If the contest is not made up, it would be a shame because it sounds like it would have been an entertaining contest. While the Waves are just 2-2 this season, they average 96 points per game and play a fast-paced brand of basketball.

Grizzlies forward GG Jackson sustained what coach Tuomas Iisalo called a "relatively serious foot injury" in the first quarter of the win vs the Nets. Jackson played just 2 minutes, 52 seconds before leaving the game with 5:01 to play in the first quarter. The Grizzlies later confirmed during the game that Jackson would not return because of a left foot injury. "That's very sad for him. He was catching a good stride," Iisalo said after the game. "There will be some further testing, but so far it doesn't look very good."

Texas quarterback Arch Manning had a miserable outing vs. LSU, but his final pass of the day, a touchdown, proved the difference-maker vs. the Tigers. Trailing No. 22 LSU on the road by five, 21-16, and facing a second-and-goal from the Tigers' 4-yard line with six seconds remaining, Arch Manning found an outbreaking Raleek Brown for a 4-yard touchdown pass with two seconds left to give the No. 8 Longhorns a dramatic 22-21 victory on Saturday, Nov. 14 at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. It marked the final play of a 12-play, 58-yard drive that helped coach Steve Sarkisian's team earn a win in a game in which they trailed by 11 with two minutes remaining in the third quarter.

(AP) — Micah Ford rushed for 149 yards and three touchdowns and Stanford’s defense forced three turnovers to lead the Cardinal to a 40-22 victory over Virginia Tech on Saturday.The Cardinal (5-5, 3-4 Atlantic Coast Conference), who scored their most points in an ACC game since joining the league, snapped a 15-game road losing streak, which was the longest in school history and had been the longest active streak in FBS. Virginia Tech (6-4, 3-4) entered the game as 15.5-point favorites according to BetMGM Sportsbook, but the Hokies turned the ball over three times in the first half, fell behind 21-0, and never recovered in losing their second consecutive game.

(AP) — Baylor Haynes threw for 309 yards and two touchdowns and Tulsa never trailed in a 38-21 win over Florida Atlantic on Saturday night to become eligible for a bowl game.Javon Ross had 163 yards on six receptions, Damari Alston ran for 92 yards on 11 carries and scored a touchdown, and Trequan Jones scored twice on the ground for Tulsa (6-4, 3-3 American Conference). Caden Veltkamp threw for 340 yards and two touchdowns, completing 32 of 58 passes for FAU (6-4, 3-3). Haynes threw a 5-yard touchdown to Jimmy Calloway with 1:47 left in the first quarter for the game's first score. Tulsa made it 14-0 early in the second when Haynes threw a 9-yard score to Calloway.

The petition had attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.
